# Andrews and Grammar OS: grammatical topology

This is a lesson index and a comparison at the level of representative contrasts. An indexed lesson is not a verified public route. Canvas supplies the analysis, the Atoms index evidence, and the canonical Owners license constructions.

The mathematical interpretation used here has three independent coordinates: positions in the realized expression, containment of grammatical units, and typed links between units or their positions. A constituent can occupy several positions. Derivational ancestry and workspace history are separate relations.

## Intention

Understand the organization Andrews identifies in Classical Nahuatl and establish where Grammar OS preserves it. Begin each contrast with the relationship in Canvas. That relationship determines which examples to compare, which features must stay fixed, and what evidence answers the question. Inspect the implementation when it can explain a loss of that relationship. Once the first loss and any independent downstream gaps are evidenced, proceed to the next unresolved relationship. A verified upstream block establishes a disposition for the comparison.

- Atom `ACI-P155-L016-6D0D6602D8` records the ambiguity condition. `ACI-P155-L021-DF45DBF016` and `ACI-P155-L021-44295FD995` record the two Peter readings.

- [Canvas §17.4](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L5940): Ōquittac Petoloh has identical spelling and constituent order under two head-contact assignments. Peter shares the principal's subject referent in one and its object referent in the other. Peter is the subject of the supplementary NNC in both.

[Supplementation checks](../../src/core/sentence/supplementation.mjs#L6803) distinguish reference compatibility from selected linear order. The controller probe authorized both readings by changing only the head role.
- [History](../../src/application/classical/grammar_workspace_history.mjs#L296) records semantic dependencies separately from temporal steps. History parentage cannot establish who saw whom.
- Focused current check: `node --test src/tests/reader_51_3_embedded_possessor_contact.test.mjs src/tests/reader_56_5_tla_tlalixcapan_blueprint.test.mjs src/tests/construction_number_codec.test.mjs` yielded 6 passes and 1 failure, the §51.3 capture failure above.

### Further clause, derivation, and reading contrasts

**Attested compound pair (§§31.3, 31.7).** Andrews's governed **ā-cal-li** has water as embed and house/enclosure as governing matrix. His balanced **ā-l-tepē-tl** has water and hill as equal conjuncts, with a vestige of the first conjunct's number-position morph. See [Canvas §31.3](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L11136), [§31.7](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L11381), and Atoms `ACI-P295-L007-5A83E8E98A`, `ACI-P295-L010-EFDED00543`, and `ACI-P300-L036-AA3E8FF2B3-03`. A fresh runtime call to `evaluateClassicalNahuatlNominalConstruction` authorized both: **Ācalli.** reported `matrixGovernsClass: true` and class source `matrix`; **Āltepētl.** reported `matrixGovernsClass: false`, class source `second-conjunct`, and vestige `l`. Second-conjunct class selection does not turn the second member into a governing matrix. This Owner probe is separate from public Grammar/Analysis/replay proof.

**§§31.3 and 31.7 Analysis and replay boundary.** The accepted **Āltepētl.** screenshot contains both the Owner-derived cue “equal first-conjunct plus second-conjunct” and a generic Lesson 31 cue calling `tepē` the grammatical head. The latter is inserted for the authorized nominal-compound operation kind without testing whether the matrix governs. Linear therefore carries the balanced analysis and a contradictory headship claim. Both Diagram views show nounstem and number-connector material; the receipts do not verify a diagrammatic edge distinguishing government from balance. The address shown after both live Results decodes to an `nnc:embed-matrix` source with two empty stem/class pairs, default `integrated`, no constituent slots, and an empty application-level structure choice. The source projector takes lexical coordinates from captured constituent Results. The operation replay adapter requires both constituent dependencies and returns null without them. This explains why that shared payload cannot reconstruct either exact compound even though it decodes. Whether **Āltepētl.** republished the same payload or kept the earlier URL remains unverified. [Live Linear and Diagram](/tmp/worker8094-attested-final-captures.txt) · [Fresh replay](/tmp/worker8094-attested-balanced-replay.txt) · [Generic Linear cue](../../src/ui/rendering/formula_presentation.mjs#L1892) · [Source projection](../../src/owner/classical/source_construction_adapters.mjs#L83) · [Replay dependency guard](../../src/owner/classical/nnc_construction_adapters.mjs#L75)

**Included versus shared reference (§19.3.1).** Andrews gives **Nelli in ōniquihtoh.** both analyses. In the included reading, the entire adjoined VNC supplies the NNC's subject referent. In the shared reading, the adjoined object's `qu` shares reference with that subject. Atoms `ACI-P168-L003-5D4CB4C05C-04`, `-06`, and `-09` record the distinction and ambiguity. [Canvas §19.3.1](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L6437)

Whether those projections display each contrast is still **unverified**.

**Source-to-Grammar boundary.** The Apply button and Enter both call the forced Source commit. For a committable replacement it clears the Result continuation, refreshes the surface and rebuilds the navigator. The Source editor and navigator read separate state. The navigator can prefer a retained review Result, a continued capture or an exact continued Source over a typed frame from the new surface. The Grammar caption is derived from the validated navigator's exact input, so the stale caption identifies a stale live binding. In the §49.2a receipt the Source also reverted immediately to the accepted Result; in the §57.1 receipt the Overview still named the new draft. Enter independently reproduced §49.2a. The later live debugger traces below identify the restoring branch. Decoding the emitted **Chīhualo** address confirms that the VNC adapter stores lexical `chīhua`, specific-projective Source and object kind, first-singular subject, indicative and present. ## Remaining contrast dispositions

### Lessons 1–3: phonological input and grammatical boundary authority

The [Canvas](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md) and Atoms `ACI-P021-L026-83890507C7` and `ACI-P039-L003-5036476036` distinguish the carrier from what it bears and the phoneme inventory from written realization. This distinction is testable at the Writing Source boundary. A fresh run of the Lesson 1 and Lessons 2–3 fixtures and the Writing Source contract reported 11 passes and 3 failures. The Owner tests preserve the contrast between a raw whole sound sequence and an issued grammatical Source with morph boundaries. Raw sound permits ordinary Writing, whereas the exact grammatical Source can license its boundary-specific optional alternatives. The required `n+p` fixture reached the exact mandatory written form while keeping the original phonemes; its later invalidation assertion failed. The Source Apply test failed while extracting a function from the current source file, before running Apply. The other failed parent-custody assertion leaves revalidation **unverified**. A fresh 8094 browser census found no public Writing entry in Source or Grammar, and a separate fresh session verified the same absence after replaying and continuing an accepted VNC. The hidden transcription controls did not expose a public route in these states. On those checked paths the first public stop is Writing Source or operation admission; paired Make, formats and replay are **blocked upstream**. The Owner’s phoneme and licensed morph-boundary distinction remains independently demonstrated by the runtime fixture. [Fresh public entry census](/tmp/topology-1-3-public-census.out) · [Accepted VNC continuation census](/tmp/topology-1-3-public-result.out). **§§1.4–1.5, carrier and content versus levels of analysis.** Andrews distinguishes the carrier medium from semantic content, then applies type, token and instance across the systems. Atom `ACI-P021-L026-83890507C7` records the communication structure. The foundation code preserves these as separate axes: phoneme/phone/sound and grapheme/graph/letter are carrier-side examples, while sememe/seme/meaning are content-side examples. Its grammar-route validation separately requires a language-specific Owner. Running the full Lesson 1 fixture with the current runtime passed all 50 assertions. The foundation distinction itself is not a selectable clause operation, so a standalone Grammar Make, Linear, Diagram and replay are **not applicable** to it. ### Lesson 4: shared subject discontinuity and distinct predicate domains

Canvas §§4.2–4.4 distinguishes VNC and NNC predicate structure while requiring a shared discontinuous Subject: person precedes the predicate and number follows it. Atom `ACI-P060-L007-CD8DC4B7D1-02` indexes the nuclear-clause domain. The retained server Make and replay snapshots for first-singular **Ninemi** show `#ni-0(nemi)0+0-0#` in Linear and one Diagram Subject row containing the two separated subject positions around the ellipsis. The predicate stem is **Core**. The retained **Cuāuhtli.** Make and replay show `#0-0(cuāuh)tli-0#`, with Subject and Predicate in Diagram and the nounstem’s `tli` position adjoining the final subject slot. Together the public controls verify that the formats preserve the shared bracketed subject and distinguish the predicate domains. They verify only the observed singular cells. The §15.1.1 possessive plural replay limitation below remains separate. A failed reconstruction and an absent address are different observations.

### Diagnostic priority across verified mismatches

The order follows dependency: admission and accepted Result first, then structural representation and portability. A mismatch in a later layer still stands when another public route reaches that layer. The acceptance checks in the table above apply to each entry. The [selected first slice](#first-implementation-slice-selected) follows this order and uses the §17.4 calibration as its acceptance test.

1. **Public input and Make.** Exact Source admission (§49.2a), stale Source-to-Grammar identity (§49.2a and §57.1), unstaged place formation (§48.1), and the Add edit's revision guard (§17.4) all prevent the intended Owner request from executing on the affected routes. In §18.4, the captured inner Result reaches outer Compose, where the controller-bound Subject identities fail the Owner’s shared-reference guard. The direct purpose marker picker (§50.6.1) blocks separate marker capture, and the pre-marked adjunct route makes the complete sentence. The cardinal prerequisite (§55.1) and relationless noun-first matrix probe (§56.5) stop their tested assemblies before Make.
2. **Grammar choice updates.** The §31.7 Structure control misses the raw nominal writer in both directions. The visible nominalization selectors in §§36 and 40.11, classifier and count selectors in §34.6, action-noun choices in §37.5, and perfective patientive choices in §39.1 miss the generic change guard. The §38.1 patientive controls miss a separate root-stock guard, and the §39.2 control dispatches the stale root-stock request. These cases leave stale executable proposals. §37.5 operation restaging reaches the writer but cannot supply the Owner-authorized variant through Grammar. The visible hui selector in §54.2.2 misses a third guard and never synchronizes Stem shape. The §39.8 subjectless route shares the generic Family staging failure. Restaging makes its absolutive, then a separate State guard resets the possessive selection. The linked traces distinguish these failures by the first missing state transition.
3. **Structural Analysis.** Current Peter replay preserves both contact endpoints in Linear and Diagram (§17.4). Whole-clause inclusion is implicit even when Shared contact displays for the same marked sentence (§19.3.1). The collective agreement cue is lost despite visible number-slot differences (§18.5), and preposed topic rank is lost despite visible written order (§17.5). The included-possessor contact is absent from public Analysis (§51.3.3.b). The §18.4 direct Analysis projection retains prefix attachment but leaves the reused VNC’s outer role and the inner Possessor contact implicit. The short-pronoun clause roles and shared Subject contact appear, while the composite annotation walk drops the whole-frame standalone restriction (§18.2). The Type Three compound has Linear but no typed Diagram projection (§39.7.2.b). The earlier balanced compound displayed a governing head in Linear (§31.7). The later restaged build and its replay preserve equal conjuncts in both formats. Current §43.3 public Make and replay retain both discontinuous orders and role labels.
4. **Portable construction identity.** Proximal, distal and unmarked **aqi** collide (§49.2a), as do all three directions within each present and preterit group (§57.1), as do the two Spanish plural connectors (§57.1). The admonitive `in` and `ih` pair collapses at descriptor projection (§10.2). The public **Ninihtoa / Ninohtoa** pair also collapses there, despite distinct recoverable History entries (§2.6). The actorless **Necōz** route loses its authenticated nonactive carrier and patient before replay (§20.8). Both finite and sentence addresses reject at the finite dependency. The finite VNC projection also loses selected causative and applicative formations (§§24.5–24.8 and §58.8). In the public `pil-ca` control, replay keeps future tense and applies it to the restored base instead of the derived stem. Directional replay silently changes the Result; the shared plural URL rejects. The §56.5 matrix loses its `tla-` formation at VNC blueprint projection. The historical Peter failures are superseded for the direct Combine Results route. The exact marked §19.3.1 pair still falls outside the supplementation adapter’s shared-contact profile. The Type Three compound requires a portable possessed patientive parent and a descriptor for the verbal matrix (§39.7.2.b). These findings have distinct acceptance checks even where the projection boundary is shared.

Visibility of a particular control, independent contact choices, address replay, and History portability follow the layer evidence recorded for that route. Typed links preserve a contact even when the same letters appear. ## Candidate topology on Andrews-licensed analyses

Andrews supplies the distinctions in the preceding comparison. The choice of points and opens below is a mathematical model of those distinctions.

Let $X$ consist of complete Andrews-licensed analyses, identified up to renaming internal node IDs. An analysis specifies typed grammatical units, their constituent roles and relations, referential contact between identified positions, and realization order and marking. History, interface state, and address strings are outside point identity. Distinct realized orders can be distinct points even where a structural observation holds of both.

An observation is a finite conjunction of evidenced grammatical constraints. Each constraint can bind a constituent by its role, attach a dependent within a specific containing unit, fix contact endpoints, or constrain realization. Shared variables must keep the same referent across the conjunction. A complete analysis extends an observation if it satisfies all its constraints. For two independently phrased observations, rename unrelated local variables apart before conjoining them. A written form is an optional observation at the realization layer.

For each observation $p$, let $U_p = \{x \in X : x \text{ extends }p\}$. Include the empty conjunction and allow incompatible conjunctions. Then $U_\top=X$, an incompatible conjunction yields the empty set, and $U_p\cap U_q=U_{p\land q}$. Arbitrary unions of these basic opens form a topology. Compatibility requires a common licensed extension. The absence of an explicit contradiction in a pair of observations alone leaves compatibility open.

### Separation and what the topology can establish

On a finite witness set, if each point is distinguishable from each other point by an observation holding at the first point, finite intersections isolate every point. The induced topology is then discrete. In particular, exact written-form observations distinguish the distinct surfaces in the three calibration cases, and contact observations split the Peter homographs. The induced topology on those six points is discrete. That test cannot establish that the full set of analyses is discrete. On the full space, a point is isolated precisely when some finite conjunction of supported observations singles it out among all licensed analyses. This remains open.

Keep the named basic observations alongside the topology. A discrete subspace admits arbitrary relabeling of its points, so a homeomorphism alone can swap subject and object and still pass. Agreement requires preservation of the **named** observations, including what they say about Andrews’s grammar.

### Discreteness of the full analysis space

For a written form $w$, let $X_w$ be the set of analyses with exactly that realization. When exact written forms are allowed observations, each $X_w$ is open. Its complement is the union of the other written-form opens, so $X$ is the topological disjoint union of these surface fibers. In particular, $X$ is discrete exactly when each fiber is discrete in its induced topology. If every fiber is finite and each of its analyses can be separated from every competing analysis by an observation in the required direction, $X$ is discrete. A proof of finite ambiguity and separation for all licensed forms is still missing.

Andrews's §17.4 gives a boundary for point identity. He groups “Peter saw him” and “Peter saw her” under the same subject-contact reading, and “He saw Peter” and “She saw Peter” under the same object-contact reading. For this contrast, the English choices express contextual possibilities within a point. They supply no evidence of an additional grammatical coordinate in Nahuatl. His two translations of **Ōquimittaqueh yehhuāntin.** are identical in English, yet he retains the two readings by contact. Thus neither English-gloss identity nor English-gloss difference can decide equality of points. [Canvas §17.4](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L5940)

A second topology on the same points can be generated using only structural observations, omitting exact surface, realized order, and marking. On the §43.3 pair restricted to the documented shared roles and discontinuity, this gives the indiscrete topology. Restoring the named realization observations gives the discrete topology on that pair. On the §17.4 pair, contact is structural, so those same two choices of observation families both separate the readings. This is a witness-level comparison of two topologies. Whether the structure-only topology is strictly coarser globally depends on the adopted structural vocabulary and remains open. Keep the realization observations in the agreement test so a change in order can be detected even when the chosen structural observations agree. [§43.3 paired Results](#peter-contact-discontinuous-modifier-scope-and-place-versus-gentilic)

### How to compare a Grammar OS layer in both directions

For the verified domain, let $f_L$ send an Andrews analysis to its observed representation in layer $L$. Fix the route and context when observations differ by route. A missing address leaves replay undefined for the corresponding point.

Every observation in layer $L$ should pull back to the Andrews observation it claims to express. Conversely, every required Andrews observation on the tested domain should be the pullback of the corresponding named observation in $L$. A pair collapsed by $f_L$ cannot satisfy the second condition for an observation that separates the pair. An extra governing-head label fails the first condition if Andrews’s balanced analysis has no governing head at that node. When comparing a fresh replay, require it to reproduce the original point as identified by the supported observations. A success status and matching surface alone leave that identity unproved.

On the verified witness pairs, the Owner preserves the listed contact, compound role, and order observations in both directions. The early Peter formats failed the contact completeness check and the early balanced compound failed the governing-head soundness check. The later verified routes preserve both sets of observations. §43.3 Linear preserves the two order observations. Its role display is verified in conjunction with the Result role labels. Absent whole diagrams and addresses leave those comparisons undefined.

Use the same scoped observation on both sides of the comparison. Within a declared test domain, let $T$ be the set of Andrews points satisfying it, $P$ the points where the layer explicitly affirms it, and $N$ the points where the layer explicitly denies it. A field in an exhaustive choice supports an explicit denial when it records the mutually exclusive alternative. Silence or conflicting cues leave truth at the layer unresolved. Require soundness ($P\subseteq T$ and $N\subseteq D\setminus T$) and complete determination ($P=T$ and $N=D\setminus T$) where the layer is expected to express both values. Keep positive and negative claims separate when both appear for the same analysis, so a contradictory display fails the soundness check. Track route coverage independently of these comparisons.

### Grammatical points and workspace histories

A route can reach the same grammatical point through different histories. Conversely, one history can successively contain distinct grammatical points. Model each accepted history entry by its projection to the issued analysis. The inverse image of a grammatical open consists of all entries whose accepted analysis satisfies that observation. An observation about the previous entry belongs to the history itself. It describes a grammatical open only if it is invariant across all histories that issue the same analysis.

On the §17.4 recovery trace, entry 4 is the subject reading, and entry 5 is the object reading. Entry 5 follows entry 4 in History, but the object reading still takes the marked **Ōquittac.** and the nominal **Petoloh.** as its grammatical constituents. “Contains the earlier subject reading” would give the wrong answer for entry 5. The exact objects reopened from History retain their separate Owner endpoints, while the reopened Linear and Diagram collide. Recovery within the workspace therefore preserves more observations than either displayed format. Whole address replay remains undefined for both entries. [History state and exact recovery](#current-calibration-by-layer) · [Live reopen trace](/tmp/worker8094-17-4-history-reopen-cdp.txt)

Acceptance requires reopening each same-surface History entry and checking its contact endpoints against the exact Owner analysis. Repeat with the readings made in the opposite order to verify that only History order changes. The reversed public order completed on 8094: build 4 became Object contact and build 5 became Subject contact. Reopening each showed its own endpoint in Linear and Diagram. The two emitted addresses continued to distinguish the readings. [Reversed Make order and History recovery](/tmp/topology-peter-reversed-history-formats.json)

### Address collisions and recoverable opens

On a verified route domain $D$, let $e:D\to A$ assign the emitted address and let $r$ be fresh replay on the addresses where it succeeds. Addresses are observed as discrete values here. Character similarity and number-theoretic encoding do not supply a notion of grammatical neighborhood.

An observation $U\subseteq D$ is recoverable from address alone exactly when it is a union of fibers of $e$. If $U=e^{-1}(V)$ for some set of addresses $V$, all points at any one address agree about $U$. Conversely, if all points at each address agree, take $V=e(U)$. To recover an entire analysis, require $r(e(x))=x$ on the declared support domain. An address collision between distinct points makes this impossible for any deterministic replay. A replay error is a separate failure even if the address identifies a unique point.

The §49.2a Class B present control witnesses all three cases at one address. Let $D=\{h,o,a\}$ for **Huālaqi**, **Onaqi**, and **Aqi**. Grammar, Linear and Diagram distinguish the directional choices. The independent address receipts give $e(h)=e(o)=e(a)$, and fresh replay gives $r(e(h))=a$. The three directional observations are singleton opens on $D$. The only observations recoverable from address alone in this test are the empty and full subsets of $D$. Present tense holds throughout $D$ and survives replay. The constant address map on this test is continuous, so continuity in the encoding direction alone would pass despite loss of both directional readings. Named pullbacks and the replay identity check detect the loss.

Acceptance requires three distinct emitted addresses, fresh replay preserving the present tense, and the corresponding proximal, distal or unmarked observation in the reconstructed analysis. ### Nested relation counterexample

§50.5 distinguishes consideration from included-referent supplementation (§19.3). For a nested adjunct, a relation observation must identify the constituent that owns the relation. The constraint “some relation is place” can hold of both a consideration construction with an inner place relation and a construction with place at the root. Use separate constraints for the outer relation and for the relation inside its adjunct. The observation of the ordered written segments can hold for both analyses. [Canvas §50.5](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L21333) · [Nested Owner and public evidence](#lessons-4053-outstanding-layer-dispositions)

The controlled **Xontlachiye cān ye huītzeh.** pair tests this directly. The direct consideration fixture and public outer-place control have the same written form and Linear sequence. The public consideration candidate picker omitted the saved exact nested adjunct. A fresh run of the matched Owner decision contract again authorized outer place and rejected outer consideration with `classical-clause-relation-consideration-owner-incompatible`. The first restriction precedes the controller’s decision. The availability rank helper sees the exact nested adjunct’s transported relation `place` and degree `second`, then returns ranks only for that inherited relation. The observed availability contract consequently advertises only place. The consideration branch has neither a special use nor an available rank for these inputs, so the controller rejects it before constructing the direct Owner request. [Candidate facts and ranks](/tmp/topology-44-outer-ranks.out) · [Rank helper](../../src/core/clause/adjunction/adjunction.mjs#L2215) · [Consideration availability filter](../../src/core/clause/adjunction/adjunction.mjs#L4033) The direct fixture and controller therefore have different domains. Comparing only the intersection of those domains would hide the missing consideration point. Record domain coverage before testing preservation of named observations. The public Linear observation can be checked for written order on the accepted place point. The same-surface Owner comparison shows why that sequence alone cannot certify the outer relation. [Fresh contract evidence](/tmp/topology-44-topological-check.out) · [Controller recheck](/tmp/topology-44-controller-recheck.out) · [Public outer-place control](/tmp/topology-44-can-outer-place.json)

Acceptance requires the public consideration picker to accept the same exact nested adjunct as the direct Owner fixture under the attested conditions. With both constructions made, the outer labels must differ and the inner place relation must survive in both. Check those two path-scoped observations in Linear, Diagram and fresh replay. Preserve the order observation independently.

### Obligatory conditions and tendencies

An obligatory grammatical implication $p\Rightarrow q$ appears in this model as an inclusion $U_p\subseteq U_q$, with both predicates scoped to the same unit. The implication can be tested by looking for an analysis in $U_p\setminus U_q$. An empty result on a finite witness set supplies a scoped check. Andrews's wording supplies the evidence for generalizing the implication.

- **§17.5, topic and placement.** Andrews defines the topic as an adjunct standing before the principal. The topic open is therefore contained in the intersection of the adjunct and preposed opens. With exact **niPetoloh** and **nicuīca**, both public orders preserve subject contact, and only **NiPetoloh nicuīca.** has the issued topic-comment relation. The generic Diagram label Adjunct is true of both and leaves the narrower topic observation implicit. Acceptance checks the same contact in both orders and makes topic status visible only for the preposed topic. [Canvas §17.5](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L5946) · [Paired public results](#lessons-119-remaining-contrast-evidence)
- **§49.10.4, interrogative force and rank.** Andrews makes initial position obligatory for the interrogative adverbial NNC discussed there. The interrogative observation is therefore contained in the corresponding initial-position open. He describes promotion to principal rank as a tendency. The model keeps rank independently observable and introduces no universal inclusion for promotion. The marked **Īc** fixture witnesses the intersection of interrogative force, initial position and promotion. The controller controls verify the conditions of that specific route. They do not decide whether all licensed interrogative analyses are promoted. The explicit **quēn** exception requires a test that keeps lexical identity and marker choice separate. [Canvas §49.10.4](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L21118) · [Controller and constituent evidence](#lessons-4053-outstanding-layer-dispositions)

These cases check different uses of the same topology. An explicit implication constrains which points can belong to an open. A tendency needs evidence about usage or frequency beyond membership alone.

### Observations about licensed continuation

A licensed continuation can be a named observation of a source analysis. For a particular Andrews operation, the observation holds when that analysis meets the operation's grammatical source conditions. This introduces no dependence on which button was clicked or whether the public picker supports the operation. Those are separate checks of route coverage. When the operation's domain is known only through selected witnesses, record the membership of those witnesses without inferring that the whole domain is open in the previously chosen structural vocabulary. If needed, include the specific grammatical licensing predicate among the generators.

**§55.1, temporal `tiā`.** The issued numeral-day compound and the ordinary typed `cem-ilhui` control both produce **Cemilhuitl.** and share the written Linear core. The exact compound contains the numeral and day constituents and licenses the temporal conversion. The ordinary typed control lacks that relation. A fresh run of the Owner test authorized the exact compound and confirmed rejection of the ordinary control as temporal source. The ordinary build and its address replay also omit the temporal option in public Grammar. Their replay is faithful to the ordinary analysis. The exact public compound is separately blocked at cardinal capture, so absence of the temporal choice after ordinary replay cannot establish its absence for the licensed compound. [Canvas §55.1](../../ANDREWS_TRANSCRIPTION_CANVAS.md#L23757) · [Fresh Owner test](/tmp/topology-55-continuation-observation.out) · [Public typed and replay control](/tmp/topology-55-typed-day-class.out)

Acceptance requires building the compound from **Cē.** and **Ilhuitl.**, restoring those two grammatical constituents in analysis and on fresh replay, and exposing temporal `tiā` from the restored compound. The ordinary typed homograph must continue to lack that operation. Compare the shared surface observation separately.

### Model decision and evidence boundary

Use the topology generated by named grammatical observations as the comparison model. Preserve those names when comparing layers. The calibration pairs show why each part matters: contact separates identical surfaces, compound government is scoped to a particular root, and written order can vary while constituent roles remain fixed. The derivation and nested-clause checks add two requirements. A model must preserve the exact grammatical source conditions of continuations and scope a relation to the unit that bears it.

The conclusion for Grammar OS is **partial agreement on the verified routes**. Owner frames preserve the calibration distinctions. Public Analysis can omit a true claim or add a false one. Address replay has verified failures of both coverage and identity. The [acceptance checks](#first-blockers-and-acceptance-checks) specify what each affected layer must preserve. This decision adopts a comparison method. Full-space discreteness, untested Canvas constructions, and unverified public routes remain explicit open questions.
